title: Putin declares a 32-hour Orthodox Easter truce
body:
On 9 April 2026, the Kremlin announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin had declared an Easter truce lasting about a day and a half. The ceasefire ran from 16:00 Moscow time on 11 April until the end of 12 April 2026, the date of Orthodox Easter. Putin ordered his forces to stop hostilities during that period while remaining ready to respond to any action by the enemy. The Kremlin said it expected the Ukrainian side to follow the Russian example.

According to Ukrainska Pravda, the announcement followed an exchange earlier in spring. On 30 March, Zelensky had said Ukraine was willing to agree to an Easter ceasefire and an energy ceasefire. On 31 March, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the Kremlin would not support that proposal, citing the lack of a clear formulation.

The paper noted precedent from 2025, when Putin declared a three-day Easter truce from the evening of 19 April to midnight on 21 April, and Russia carried out a drone attack on Ukraine on 19 April of that year. Both sides have commonly accused each other of violating such short truces.
